title: River scene template and food chain cards
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Soils and aquatic plants (Flow and One Planet, Our World)
source: Seeded from science/y3 lesson 33 (River scene template and food chain cards (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 33: Living things that depend on rivers. To understand how living things in and near rivers depend on the water and on each other

cards:
river
fresh water flowing to the sea

adaptation
a feature that helps a living
thing survive

ecosystem
living things and their home
working together

food chain
shows what eats what
blocks.task: use them to test yourself or a partner.

questions.q: Make a food chain: heron, water plant, small fish.
questions.a: Water plant to small fish to heron
questions.model: Start with the plant: it makes its own food. What eats plants? The small fish. What eats the fish? The heron.

questions.q: Why does a fish need gills?
questions.a: To take oxygen from the water

questions.q: Name one bird that depends on rivers.
questions.a: For example: heron, kingfisher or duck

questions.q: Draw a river scene with four living things. Label one adaptation for each.
questions.a: For example: fish (gills), duck (webbed feet), heron (long legs), reeds (grow at the edge)
questions.model: Teacher draws a duck and labels 'webbed feet: push through water'.

questions.q: Draw a food chain with four links from your river.
questions.a: For example: water plants to snail to fish to heron

questions.q: If all the snails died, what would happen to the fish and the plants?
questions.a: Fish would have less food; plants might grow more because nothing eats them.

questions.q: A duck's webbed feet are an...
Big question: who is in trouble first if a river dries up?
questions.a: Fish and water plants, then the animals that eat them.
